protocol: Actual F-16 flight. The pilot heard a suspected leak while the aircraft was at 30,000 ft and selected 100% oxygen. A cabin reading of 10,000 ft was reported 10 seconds later. Earlier and peak cabin altitude and exposure duration are unavailable. Ground inspection found no defect.
outcome_window: Left-eye visual loss noticed the next morning. The abstract says presentation two days after flight. The case narrative dates the eye exam to day three. Follow-up without recurrence was reported for three years.
note: One selected case with possible DCS-related papillophlebitis. The authors also consider idiopathic papillophlebitis and other causes. The pressure excursion and clinical DCS diagnosis were unconfirmed.

protocol: Unpressurized aircraft parachute training. On 8–11 July 1986 there were three to four excursions per day to reported maxima of 11,926–12,920 ft (3,636–3,939 m), about 30 minutes each. The report states no supplemental oxygen or diving during that early period. Twenty-five additional jumps took place on 13–22 July.
outcome_window: Headache on 11 July, localization on 21 July, visual symptoms by 23 July and optometry and ophthalmology assessments on 24 July 1986. No visual recurrence was reported during the 14 months after the September 1987 follow-up.
note: One reported neurological DCS diagnosis based on this sequence and the treatment response. Exact triggering exposure and onset time are unknown. Optic neuritis remained an alternative diagnosis in the discussion.
